decision_basis: The USDA FY2024 Agency Financial Report reconciles to the same $579.36M and 2.43 percent FCIC result and defines both principal categories. Failure to access means information existed, was obtained, and was used, but an administrative or calculation error made the payment improper. Inability to access is described mainly as participant certification errors affecting insured amount, premium, or indemnity.
closure_scope: Close only the internal FY2024 FCIC root-cause taxonomy field; preserve recoverability as a separate open field.
residual_limitations: The report does not publish a complete category-level dollar split, transaction lineage, identified debt, appeal or reversal, collection, recovery, prevention attribution, or control cost.
Corrective-action descriptions do not establish collectible or recoverable amounts and do not support a savings estimate.

decision_basis: The FCIC/RMA FY2024 financial-statements report states that the improper-payment rate considers all payment categories—premium subsidy, Administrative and Operating expense, and indemnities—and separates approved insurance providers into high-, medium-, and low-payment tiers for the annual statistically valid sample. RMA COM-23-001 further states that the 326 selected policies were reviewed using applicable policyholder and approved-insurance-provider documentation through CARS.
closure_scope: Close only the FY2024 FCIC payment-universe field for internal methodology review: all three payment categories and all approved-insurance-provider payment tiers are represented by the disclosed review design.
residual_limitations: The source does not publish the sample frame, allocation, selection probabilities, weights, estimator, variance method, detailed exclusion rules, or amount-level recovery lineage.
The page-18 disclosure is in Management's Discussion and Analysis rather than the audited basic financial statements. Other Information on printed pages 60-61 is unaudited and corroborative only.
